name: Beck Scale for Suicide Ideation (BSS/BSSI)
rights: Licensed — Pearson; item text not embedded
note: 19 scored items, each 0–2. No universal validated cutoff should be used to declare an individual safe or low risk.
evidence: Pearson lists age 17+, 5–10 minute administration, manual/Q-global scoring, and five screening items.

name: Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey suicide-history items
note: History is clinically relevant but does not determine current or future risk by itself.
items: 2 binary history indicators in current prototype
evidence: Exact item provenance and wording must be frozen before item-level implementation.

name: Beck Depression Inventory-II (BDI-II)
rights: Licensed — Pearson; item text not embedded
note: Common descriptive bands: 0–13 minimal, 14–19 mild, 20–28 moderate, 29–63 severe.
evidence: Pearson lists age 13–80, 21 items, about 5 minutes, and coefficient alpha .92.

name: Perceived Stress Scale – 4 item (PSS-4)
rights: Permission/reproduction status must be confirmed before item display
note: Higher scores indicate more perceived stress; no diagnostic cutoff.
evidence: Four-item short form; two positively worded items are reverse scored. Interpret continuously rather than diagnostically.

name: Warwick–Edinburgh Mental Well-Being Scale (WEMWBS-14)
rights: Copyrighted — Warwick licence required; item text not embedded
note: Higher scores indicate greater wellbeing; interpretation is population/context dependent.
evidence: Warwick specifies 14 items scored 1–5, total 14–70, and requires an appropriate licence.

name: Defeat Scale
note: Higher scores indicate greater subjective defeat; no invented clinical cutoff.
evidence: Sixteen items, five response levels, total score 0–64; higher scores represent greater defeat.

name: Entrapment Scale
evidence: Original structure distinguishes internal and external entrapment; later studies also examine a general entrapment factor.

name: ENRICHD Social Support Instrument (ESSI)
rights: Exact deployment rights still to verify
note: Higher scores generally indicate greater perceived support.
evidence: Seven-item self-report instrument; items are summed and higher totals indicate greater social support.

name: Socially Prescribed Perfectionism subscale
rights: Author-hosted forms exist; deployment rights still to document
note: Use exact version-specific scoring and norms.
audit: AUTHOR SOURCE VERIFIED / VERSION LOCK NEEDED
evidence: Author laboratory identifies self-oriented, other-oriented, and socially prescribed perfectionism and provides scoring materials.

name: Interpersonal Needs Questionnaire (INQ-12)
note: Preserve burdensomeness and belongingness as separate subscales.
evidence: Twelve-item form is commonly scored as separate perceived-burdensomeness and thwarted-belongingness subscales.

name: Goal Adjustment Scale
evidence: Ten items on five-point responses; four form disengagement and six form reengagement.

name: Life Orientation Test – Revised (LOT-R)
rights: Exact public-reproduction status should be documented
note: 10 prompts; 6 scored and 4 fillers; negatively keyed items are reversed.
subscales: Usually optimism total; some studies separate optimism/pessimism
evidence: Six scored items contribute to the 0–24 total; four prompts are fillers and negative items are reverse keyed.

name: Connor–Davidson Resilience Scale – 10 item (CD-RISC-10)
rights: Copyright/licensing applies; item text not embedded
note: Higher scores indicate greater resilience; use population-appropriate norms.
evidence: Official CD-RISC manual specifies a 0–40 total and cautions that interpretation varies by population and location.

name: Acquired Capability for Suicide Scale (ACSS)
rights: Version and reproduction status must be verified
note: Multiple forms exist; version must be frozen before scoring and scores must not be mixed across forms.
audit: VERSION CONFLICT RESOLVED CONCEPTUALLY / DEPLOYMENT LOCK NEEDED
evidence: Ribeiro et al. retained seven fearlessness-about-death items, scored 0–4, yielding a 0–28 ACSS-FAD total with alpha .77–.83 across samples.

name: Barratt Impulsiveness Scale Version 11 (BIS-11)
rights: Verify reproduction status; use authoritative key
note: 30 items with reverse-keyed items. Treat proposed factor scores cautiously because factor structure has been challenged.
subscales: Traditional attentional, motor, nonplanning factors; interpretation contested
evidence: BIS-11 is widely used, but later factor-analytic work found poor support for the traditional three-subscale structure; v0.3 flags this rather than overclaiming subscales.

name: Exposure to Suicide / Self-Harm items
construct: Exposure through self, family, friends or others
rights: Exact source wording/version must be verified
note: Contextual exposure information is not a deterministic risk score.
evidence: Keep as contextual indicators until exact source, wording, and scoring provenance are frozen.

name: Suicide / Self-Harm Mental Imagery items
rights: Exact source and reproduction status must be verified
note: Use as a structured research/clinical signal, not as a stand-alone risk category.
evidence: Exact original source, anchors, scoring, and rights must be frozen before item-level deployment.
